scope: Review of the 13 remaining pinned skill entrypoints and their applicable per-skill LICENSE.txt files, with deeper local-support review for web-artifacts-builder and internal-comms and a harness-QA pattern review of pptx. Prioritize software-delivery and agent-workflow relevance; linked support outside those reviewed paths remains indexed-only. Third-party/font/asset and doc-coauthoring license gaps are carried forward without inference. Revision 5 records the disposition of the nine inspected entrypoints not previously in the candidate list; XLSX is a QA-pattern candidate only, and the other eight are explicitly excluded from the coding-harness candidate set.

limits: The pinned anthropics/skills tree is complete (544 entries). Revision 4 inspected the 13 previously indexed-only SKILL.md entrypoints and their per-skill LICENSE.txt files. Deep support review in this revision is limited to the web-artifacts-builder setup/bundle scripts and internal-comms examples; other linked support is indexed-only.

skill-creator quick_validate.py imports yaml, and package_skill.py imports quick_validate, but the skill tree has no PyYAML version constraint or lock. PyYAML upstream LICENSE at commit f5e4504a92f169f65350a1047dccb23bc97028be is MIT; this is not evidence that any actual installed release is that snapshot.

MCP builder requirements.txt specifies only anthropic>=0.39.0 and mcp>=1.1.0. Their exact minimum release source trees declare MIT, but those open-ended constraints do not pin the resolved versions. The inspected minimum releases declare additional ranged dependencies (httpx, pydantic, typing-extensions, anyio, distro, sniffio, jiter; and anyio, httpx, httpx-sse, pydantic, starlette, sse-starlette respectively); no resolver output, lockfile, or complete transitive license inventory is present.

The skill-creator viewer loads SheetJS 0.20.3 from a CDN with an SRI digest. The GitHub v0.20.3 tag lookup returned 404; the available SheetJS GitHub branch snapshot at commit 3f44ddd99c704d7ca35ea76fef7b8af2d2d435cb is package version 0.18.12 under Apache-2.0, so it does not clear the different CDN artifact. No CDN request was made.

Google Fonts upstream OFL 1.1 terms were inspected for Poppins and Lora at google/fonts commit 5bd87dfc525c8a0d1d8529d3684716e00c3fc59a. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists Lora but not Poppins. The CSS endpoint and delivered font files are dynamic and not pinned by the source HTML; the upstream license-file evidence does not hash the served font binaries.

The TypeScript MCP implementation guides are references, not shipped package manifests. They provide example SDK/Zod dependencies but no concrete package lock or selected SDK release; license applicability for an implementation built from those guides remains unresolved. External sources were accessed only via read-only GitHub APIs; no external CDN or other non-GitHub URL was fetched.

The 13 reviewed skill LICENSE.txt files all state Apache License 2.0; this is only a skill-level grant. It does not license framework packages, fonts, scripts, media, or other bundled assets. No dependency or asset license was inferred for support not inspected.

web-artifacts-builder directly installs a large, dynamically versioned React/Vite/Tailwind/shadcn dependency set and its bundle script adds Parcel packages. The pinned source tree does not contain the shadcn-components.tar.gz required by init-artifact.sh, nor a package manifest/lock; the skill says visual testing is optional and may occur after sharing. These scripts were read only and not executed.

internal-comms examples provide writing templates but no connectors or provenance/security policy for Slack, email, Drive, or calendar access. Treat those sources as separately authorized inputs; no external data sources were accessed.

The pptx entrypoint prescribes content, structural, and visual QA with helper scripts, but those helper implementations/dependency licenses were not deeply inspected in this scope. PDF, DOCX, XLSX, creative-art, and Slack-GIF linked helpers/assets likewise remain indexed-only except files already reviewed in earlier revisions.

Revision 5 selectively inspected XLSX recalc.py and office/soffice.py for outcome reporting and runtime boundaries. Other XLSX support, runtime licensing and portability are not verified; neither helper is proposed for adoption.
